_readme: [pipeline 7]P-10 — no production pack is signed before key custody is drill-proven.
🔴 THE ORIGINAL ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS DROPPED, NOT SATISFIED. It demanded a recorded restore
FROM SHARES drill. [ADR 022] (LOCKED 2026-07-27) states that Shamir splitting is NOT required:
there are no shares, there never will be, and splitting was rejected precisely because it puts a
tool dependency in the restore path — the same trap [ADR 021] and [1]F-7b exist to remove. A
criterion naming an artifact a locked decision abolished is permanently unsatisfiable. Correct the
evidence, not the decision.
WHAT REPLACES IT: tooling/content_pipeline/src/sign.mjs REFUSES a production key_id unless this
file records a dated restore drill for it. That refusal runs LOCALLY, never in CI — the seed must
never reach a runner, so CI signs as the derived `test-k1` and the production canary is owner-run.
assert-publish-gate.mjs PRINTS the gap on every CI run instead of failing, because a guard that
blocks all CI on work only the owner can physically do is a guard somebody switches off.
WHAT A DRILL IS, exactly (it is short): take each stored copy IN TURN — .claude/pack-signing.seed
and the printed paper copy — restore the seed from it alone, sign a message with the restored key,
and verify that signature through the production Ed25519PackVerifier against the k1 pinned in
packages/core/lib/src/content/pack_verifier.dart. Then write today's date into drilled_on below.
Two copies that fail differently are only two copies once BOTH have been read back.
⚠️ THE PAPER COPY IS ALSO STILL OWED and this file does not pretend otherwise. [ADR 022]'s own
'What is still owed' section says so: until it exists the seed has one copy plus a backup sharing
one Google account, which is the failure that ADR spends most of its length arguing against.
